message.content:
当前基线已有授权评估、决策事件、依据审计、因果追踪和问责导出。本次新增一次性执行授权凭证，把审计通过的允许事件转为短期且只能消费一次的票据；既有行为不变，旧库和空库继续可用。

新增 POST /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-grants，请求体只含 event_id 与 1 到 300 的非布尔整数 ttl_seconds。event_id 指向路径机器 allowed=true、reason=allowed_by_policy 且依据审计 valid 的事件。非法请求体为 422 invalid_grant_request，额外查询为 422 invalid_query，缺失或跨机器对象为 404 not_found；事件非允许、无历史依据、依据失败分别为 409 event_not_allowed、409 decision_basis_unavailable、409 decision_basis_invalid。每事件限签一次，并发仅一个成功，其余 409 grant_already_exists。成功 201 返回 {id,machine_id,event_id,issued_at,expires_at,status}，status 为 active，expires_at 是签发时刻加 ttl_seconds 的 UTC Z 时刻。

新增 POST /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-grants/{grant_id}/consume，仅接受空查询和空请求体，原子消费未用且未到期的凭证，返回 200 的 {grant_id,use_id,consumed_at}，并发消费恰好一次成功。缺失或跨机器对象为 404 not_found，已消费、到期分别为 409 grant_consumed、409 grant_expired，非空查询或请求体为 422 invalid_query。凭证和使用记录持久化、限消费一次、不可撤销续期或转移，失败无半条记录，跨重启稳定；再次签发、消费或以既有查询入口读取事件和依据时，都能稳定观察到上述结果，既有决策链、依据、审计、问责数据不重写。

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

393	class WriteTransactionDiagnostic(Base):
394	    """One read-only diagnostic record per joint-write transaction attempt.
395	
396	    A joint write is one of the two public mutating operations serialized by
397	    the same machine write lock: a machine status change (``op = "change"``)
398	    and an authorization decision-event creation (``op = "event"``). The
399	    table is append-only observability: the records are written in their own
400	    transaction(s), never updated or deleted, and never participate in
401	    authorization evaluation. Columns store only operational metadata — no
402	    keys, secrets, policy text, or identity material.

404	    * ``tid`` — stable id of the diagnostic record (a fresh UUID per attempt);
405	    * ``at`` — UTC RFC 3339 timestamp (ending in ``Z``) of the attempt's
406	      terminal outcome, also the ordering key;
407	    * ``phase`` — ``started-commit`` (the joint write committed) or
408	      ``started-rollback`` (it rolled back, with a stable failure category in
409	      ``fail``);
410	    * ``fail`` — ``none`` for committed attempts, otherwise ``race``, ``io``,
411	      or ``other``;
412	    * ``flags`` — ``[]`` or a JSON array listing ``lock_wait`` and ``retry``
413	      in the order actually experienced (a lock wait and its retries collapse
414	      into this one record);
415	    * ``status`` — the attempt's transaction terminal state: ``committed``
416	      when the joint write landed or ``rolled_back`` when it did not;
417	    * ``machine_status`` — the machine's ``active``/``suspended`` state at
418	      the terminal state, kept separate from the transaction outcome;
419	    * ``event`` — the created event id for ``op = "event"`` commits, else

from sqlalchemy import Boolean, ForeignKey, Integer, String, Text, UniqueConstraint
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class Machine(Base):
    __tablename__ = "machines"

    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(36), primary_key=True)
    external_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, unique=True, index=True, nullable=False)
    display_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)
    public_key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)
    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False, default="active")
    version: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=False, default=1)
    created_at: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)
    updated_at: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)


class MachineStatusEvent(Base):
    """One immutable machine status transition (``active`` <-> ``suspended``).

    Rows are append-only: each accepted status change inserts exactly one row
    in the same locked write transaction that updates the machine, and rows
    are never updated or deleted afterwards, so the table is a complete
    per-machine history of every committed status change. Each row also
    carries a per-machine tamper-evident hash chain
    (``previous_status_event_id``/``content_hash``/``chain_hash``) computed
    from the record identifier, ownership, status edge, and creation moment.
    """

    __tablename__ = "machine_status_events"

    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(36), primary_key=True)
    machine_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(36), ForeignKey("machines.id"), nullable=False, index=True
    )
    from_status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)
    to_status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)
    created_at: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)
    # Per-machine hash chain. Nullable so databases created before the chain
    # feature keep working; the startup migration backfills any missing values.
    previous_status_event_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(36), nullable=True)
    content_hash: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(64), nullable=True)
    chain_hash: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(64), nullable=True)


class KeyRotationEvent(Base):
    __tablename__ = "key_rotation_events"

    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(36), primary_key=True)
    machine_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(36), ForeignKey("machines.id"), nullable=False, index=True
    )
    old_public_key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)
    new_public_key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)
    version: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=False)
    created_at: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)

    transaction(s), never updated or deleted, and never participate in

      ``fail``);

    started_at: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, nullable=False)

1	# Verifiable Machine Accountability
2	
3	Backend foundation for recording, constraining, verifying, and auditing actions performed by automated systems. The service is designed to grow around machine identities, policy decisions, authorization, tamper-evident evidence, incident handling, responsibility attribution, audit queries, and compliance exports.
4	
5	## Development
6	
7	Requires Python 3.12 or newer.
8	
9	```bash
10	python -m venv .venv
11	. .venv/bin/activate
12	pip install -e '.[test]'
13	pytest -q
14	uvicorn accountability.app:app --reload
15	```
16	
17	The initial API exposes `GET /health`, which returns a JSON readiness result.
18	
19	## Authorization event integrity chain
20	
21	Each machine's authorization decision events form a per-machine, tamper-evident
22	hash chain. Every event returned by the create and list endpoints carries:
23	
24	- `previous_event_id` — `null` for the machine's first event, otherwise the id
25	  of the preceding event in `(created_at, id)` order;
26	- `content_hash` — `SHA-256(UTF-8(compact key-sorted JSON of {id, machine_id,
27	  action_type, resource, allowed, reason, created_at}))`;
28	- `chain_hash` — `SHA-256(UTF-8("" + ":" + content_hash))` for the first event
29	  and `SHA-256(UTF-8(previous_chain_hash + ":" + content_hash))` thereafter.
30	
31	All hashes are 64-character lowercase hexadecimal strings. For a decision-event
32	request, the machine/status lookup, the suspended-or-declaration/policy
33	decision, and the chain-tail append all run inside one locked write
34	transaction — the same lock the machine status-change endpoint takes — so
35	concurrent writes cannot lose events, fork, or break the chain, and a status
36	change and an event append always have one definite serial order. On startup
37	the service adds the new columns to pre-existing databases and backfills
38	missing chain data in `(created_at, id)` order; the recomputation is
39	deterministic, so restarting with an already complete database performs no
40	writes.
41	
42	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-decision-events/integrity` verifies
43	the chain read-only and returns `{valid, checked_count, broken_event_id}`:
44	a complete or empty chain reports `true`, the total count, and `null`;
45	otherwise it reports `false`, the total count, and the first event whose
46	content hash, link, or chain hash does not verify. A missing machine returns
47	`404 not_found`.
48	
49	## Immutable authorization decision basis snapshots
50	
51	Every new authorization decision event saves, in the same locked write
52	transaction that appends the event, an immutable snapshot of the basis the
53	decision was made on — the machine status, the enabled behavior declarations
54	and their matching scope, the policy candidate rules and their relations, and
55	the committed result, reason, and capture moment. The snapshot and the event
56	commit atomically or leave no trace; snapshots are append-only and are never
57	updated, recomputed, or reconstructed from later data. The real write entry
58	stays the public authorization-decision-event creation endpoint — no
59	bypassing business write entry is added. Only visible business fields are
60	stored: never machine/public keys or policy text beyond the rules' existing
61	visible columns.
62	
63	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-decision-events/{event_id}/decision-basis`
64	is the read-only query under the machine authorization decision event path;
65	the caller submits only the path machine id and event id. Any query
66	parameter, a repeated parameter, or a request body is
67	`422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_query"}}` validated before the machine, event,
68	or snapshot is read (the same malformed request against a non-existent
69	machine is still `422`). After validation, a missing machine, a missing
70	event, or an event owned by another machine returns
71	`404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}`. An event that exists but was committed
72	before this feature existed (and so has no historical snapshot) returns
73	`404 {"error":{"code":"snapshot_not_found"}}` — the basis is never fabricated
74	from current declarations or rules. Only `GET` is routed; `HEAD` and every
75	other method return `405` without reading the snapshot, recomputing a
76	decision, or writing anything. A real failure while reading the event or
77	snapshot returns `500 {"error":{"code":"internal_error"}}` with no event
78	summary and no partial basis.
79	
80	A successful response is exactly five groups in this fixed order:
81	
82	- `event_summary` — one object with the event's committed result and reason
83	  (`allowed`, `reason`), its capture moment (`created_at`), and its chain
84	  fields (`previous_event_id`, `content_hash`, `chain_hash`);
85	- `status_basis` — `{machine_id, status, captured_at, declarations_read,
86	  policies_read}`: the machine status the decision used, the capture moment,
87	  and whether declarations and policy rules were read at all. A suspended
88	  machine's snapshot records `status "suspended"` with both read flags
89	  `false` (no declarations and no policy were consulted); an active machine
90	  has `declarations_read true`, and `policies_read` is `true` only when at
91	  least one enabled declaration matched (the decision stops at
92	  `no_enabled_declaration` before the rules otherwise);
93	- `declaration_basis` — `{read, declarations}`: the machine's enabled
94	  declarations for the requested action that participated in the judgement,
95	  each carrying its visible fields `{id, action_type, resource_pattern,
96	  enabled, created_at, updated_at}` plus a boolean `matched` for whether its
97	  pattern matched the requested resource. A suspended machine records `read
98	  false` and an empty array; a disabled or other-action declaration never
99	  appears;
100	- `policy_candidates` — `{read, candidates, winners, conflicts}`. `read` is
101	  true only when the declaration gate passed. Each candidate keeps the
102	  rule's seven visible fields plus a `relation` under the existing priority
103	  semantics: `winner` (a decisive minimum-priority candidate), `overridden`
104	  (a matching candidate at a larger numeric priority), `conflict` (a
105	  minimum-priority candidate when the decisive tier mixes allow and deny;
106	  the tier is then decided as a denial), or `unmatched` (a same-action rule
107	  whose pattern did not match). Candidates are ordered by priority
108	  ascending, then by the actual UTC instant of `created_at`, then by id.
109	  `winners` lists the decisive rules as `{id, effect, priority,
110	  created_at}` and is empty for a mixed tier; `conflicts` lists that tier as
111	  id-ascending unordered pairs. Rules for other actions never participate and
112	  never appear. Every collection is present even when empty;
113	- `decision` — `{allowed, reason}`, exactly the result committed on the
114	  event; the stored basis is emitted verbatim and the decision is never
115	  recomputed, so it can never disagree with the event's stored result.
116	
117	Records are output in stable order as compact UTF-8 JSON terminated by a
118	single newline, with no floating-point, `-0.0`, or non-finite value. The
119	captured document is stored once and re-emitted byte-for-byte, so repeated
120	queries of one event are byte-identical; snapshots persist across application
121	restarts and are strictly isolated to the path machine (another machine's
122	event id on the path is a `404 not_found`). The query is strictly read-only:
123	it never creates, updates, deletes, repairs, or normalizes an event,
124	snapshot, declaration, or rule. On startup the snapshot table is created
125	safely on databases that predate the feature (an older database's existing
126	events simply answer `snapshot_not_found`), an empty database can both
127	create events and query their bases, and the event list, hash chain, evidence
128	chain, incident responsibility, privacy exports, diagnostics, and the health
129	check are unchanged.
130	
131	### Independent read-only consistency audit
132	
133	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-decision-events/{event_id}/decision-basis/integrity`
134	is the independent verification sub-entry under the snapshot path: it does not
135	re-emit the snapshot, it checks it, read-only, against the committed event. It
136	accepts only the path machine id and event id — any query parameter, a repeated
137	parameter, or a request body is
138	`422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_query"}}`, validated before the machine, event,
139	or snapshot is read (the same malformed request against a non-existent machine
140	is still `422`). After validation a missing machine, a missing event, or an
141	event owned by another machine returns
142	`404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}` with no audit conclusion. Only `GET` is
143	routed; `HEAD` and every other method return `405` without reading or writing.
144	A real failure while reading the event, snapshot, declarations, or rules
145	returns `500 {"error":{"code":"internal_error"}}` with no conclusion and no
146	partial result.
147	
148	A successful response carries exactly four conclusions in this fixed order:
149	
150	- `valid` — `true` only when the event summary, status basis, declaration
151	  basis, policy candidates, and final decision all agree with one another and
152	  with the committed event;
153	- `checked_count` — `0` when the event has no snapshot row and `1` when the one
154	  snapshot row exists (even if that snapshot is damaged). Another machine's
155	  snapshot is never counted, and there is at most one snapshot per event;
156	- `broken_basis_id` — the path event id whenever the conclusion is false,
157	  `null` on success;
158	- `reason` — `null` on success; the fixed `snapshot_not_found` for a missing
159	  row; otherwise the stable category of the first anomaly found.
160	
161	The checks verify, in a fixed order: the document parses to the five expected
162	groups with sound field types and ordering; the event summary corresponds
163	verbatim to the event's committed `allowed` result, `reason`, capture moment
164	(`created_at`), and chain fields (`previous_event_id`, `content_hash`,
165	`chain_hash`) — nothing is recomputed or filled in; the machine status is
166	reconstructed **as of the event** from the machine's own
167	`machine_status_events` transition history rather than its current row; a
168	suspended machine's basis explicitly records that declarations and policy
169	were not read, while an active machine's read flags match its status and the
170	declaration gate; the declaration basis names exactly the enabled
171	declarations that participated in that action and resource judgement (a
172	missing, disabled, other-action, or superfluous record is an inconsistency,
173	and each `matched` scope flag must be correct); the policy candidates'
174	winner/overridden/conflict/unmatched (and invalid) relations, winner group,
175	conflict pairs, and priority-first ordering must follow the priorities as of
176	the event and support the final judgement; and the final decision equals the
177	event's committed `allowed` flag and `reason`.
178	
179	The event-time status is rebuilt by an independent read of the machine's
180	transition history: only a transition whose actual creation instant is not
181	later than the capture instant (`created_at <= capture`) forms the state
182	then, same-instant transitions apply in ascending `id` order, and with no
183	qualifying transition the machine's creation default `active` carries
184	forward unchanged. A snapshot that merely agrees with the machine's current
185	status while contradicting that event-time state is rejected. The status
186	basis is judged history, then state, then read flags, giving three fixed
187	categories:
188	
189	- `status_history_invalid` — the history is misattributed, illegal, or not
190	  rebuildable: a non-text or unparseable `created_at` (the as-of boundary is
191	  undecidable), a non-text `id` (same-instant ordering unstable), a status
192	  outside `active`/`suspended`, a self edge, or a `from_status` that does not
193	  continue the state the earlier transitions establish. Every stored
194	  transition of the machine is counted, including one committed after the
195	  capture (the history is one append-only chain whose edges must continue one
196	  another); a damaged record is reported, never crashed on, repaired,
197	  rewritten, or recomputed;
198	- `status_state_mismatch` — the history rebuilds soundly but the rebuilt
199	  event-time status differs from the snapshot's recorded `status`;
200	- `read_flags_mismatch` — the state agrees but the recorded
201	  `declarations_read`/`policies_read` flags (and the declaration group's own
202	  `read` flag) contradict the gate in force then: a suspended machine reads
203	  neither declarations nor policy, an active machine reads declarations, and
204	  policy is read only when at least one enabled declaration matched.
205	
206	A real failure while reading the status history (like the event, snapshot,
207	declarations, or rules) returns `500 internal_error` with no conclusion and
208	no partial result, and no status history is ever fabricated. Relations are
209	audited against the rules and declarations that already existed when the
210	event committed, so later declarations or rules never retroactively break a
211	faithful historical snapshot; the audit never recomputes or repairs a record
212	and never fabricates a missing basis. An event without a snapshot row
213	answers `valid false`, `checked_count 0`, `broken_basis_id` equal to the
214	event id, and `reason "snapshot_not_found"`. A damaged or contradictory
215	snapshot answers `valid false`, `checked_count 1`, the event id, and the
216	stable first-anomaly category, using exactly these buckets for damaged
217	content:
218	
219	- `malformed_document` — the document does not parse (invalid JSON or a
220	  non-finite constant), does not parse to an object, or has a document-level
221	  shape anomaly: a missing, extra, or reordered top-level group, a wrong
222	  field type on any group (the event summary, status basis, declaration
223	  basis, policy candidates, or decision), an anomalous collection shape, or
224	  an anomalous set/record ordering. Every such structural or ordering
225	  anomaly collapses to this one stable category instead of naming the group;
226	- `malformed_decision` — the structure is complete but the final decision
227	  field is illegal or contradicts the event's committed result (including a
228	  decision the rebuilt basis cannot support).
229	
230	Content-level correspondence checks that are neither structural nor the
231	final decision keep their own mismatch category in examination order:
232	`event_summary_mismatch`, the status triplet (`status_history_invalid`,
233	`status_state_mismatch`, `read_flags_mismatch`, checked history then state
234	then read flags), `status_basis_mismatch`,
235	`declaration_basis_mismatch`/`declaration_match_mismatch`, and
236	`policy_candidate_mismatch`/`policy_winner_mismatch`/
237	`policy_conflict_mismatch`. The conclusion is compact
238	UTF-8 JSON in fixed field order terminated by one newline, with no
239	floating-point or non-finite value, so identical stored data audits
240	byte-for-byte identically, the result persists across restarts, and machine
241	isolation is enforced. Event creation, the event list, the hash chain,
242	evidence chain, incident responsibility, privacy exports, diagnostics, and
243	health-check semantics are unchanged.
244	
245	### Incremental decision-basis snapshot changes query
246	
247	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-decision-events/decision-basis/changes`
248	is the stable, keyset-paginated incremental view over one machine's
249	immutable decision-basis snapshots — the `changes` sub-entry under the
250	decision-basis path (a sibling of the single-snapshot query and its
251	integrity audit). It is a separate, strictly read-only audit entry point:
252	it changes neither event creation, the single-snapshot query, the
253	consistency audit, the hash chain, the privacy exports, the compliance
254	exports, diagnostics, the authorization evaluation, nor the health check,
255	and it adds no on-disk format (cursors are stateless), so old and empty
256	databases work unchanged. The caller submits only the path machine id, a
257	page size, and an optional cursor — no business filter parameters and no
258	request body. Validation completes before the machine or any snapshot is
259	read:
260	
261	- `limit` — required, a non-boolean integer from `1` to `100`. A missing,
262	  blank, fractional (e.g. `1.0`), boolean (`true`/`false`), non-decimal, or
263	  out-of-range value returns `422 {"error":{"code":"bad_limit"}}`.
264	- `cursor` — optional, an opaque string shaped
265	  `<created_at original text>|<event id>` and returned by a previous page.
266	  An empty value, a missing separator, or an empty segment returns
267	  `422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_cursor"}}`; the timestamp segment is
268	  original stored text rather than re-parsed (the split is on the last
269	  separator), because a snapshot whose stored `created_at` no longer parses
270	  stays pageable. A well-shaped cursor whose `(created_at, event id)`
271	  position cannot be located among the path machine's stored snapshots —
272	  naming another machine's snapshot, a deleted snapshot, or an event that
273	  has no snapshot — is rejected as `422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_cursor"}}`
274	  after the snapshots are read, with no partial page, so a parameter error
275	  always takes priority over the machine lookup.
276	- Any other query parameter, a repeated `limit`/`cursor`, or a request
277	  carrying a body returns `422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_query"}}` in the
278	  validation phase; every validation error is answered without reading any
279	  machine or snapshot.
280	- The path accepts `GET` only; `HEAD` and every other method return `405`
281	  without reading a snapshot, computing a page, or writing anything.
282	- A valid query against a machine that does not exist returns
283	  `404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}` carrying no records.
284	- A failure that prevents reading the snapshots or the machine, or a stored
285	  snapshot document that is no longer decodable JSON, returns
286	  `500 {"error":{"code":"internal_error"}}` with no partial page — the row
287	  is neither repaired nor skipped.
288	
289	The success object carries exactly `{machine_id, limit, records,
290	next_cursor, has_more}` in this fixed field order; the path machine id and
291	page size are echoed verbatim, and an empty database or a machine with no
292	snapshots returns the complete empty page. Only events that already have a
293	snapshot enter the page: an event committed before the basis feature (or
294	whose snapshot row is absent) is not fabricated, is not returned, and never
295	enters a cursor. Each record is exactly `{group, record}`: the fixed tag
296	`"decision_basis"` and the same five groups the single-snapshot query
297	exposes — `event_summary`, `status_basis`, `declaration_basis`,
298	`policy_candidates`, and `decision` — emitted exactly as captured, with no
299	recomputation, audit, repair, or shape normalization, so a JSON-valid but
300	tampered document is still re-emitted verbatim. Records are ordered by the
301	snapshot creation event's actual UTC instant of `created_at` and then by
302	event id ascending, so an exact-second record sorts before any
303	fractional-second record of the same second; a stored `created_at` that no
304	longer parses never crashes the query — its original text is kept and it
305	deterministically sorts after every parseable instant.
306	
307	The cursor is an exclusive position over `(created_at, event id)`: it
308	points just after a page's last snapshot, so the page returns only
309	snapshots strictly after it. Repeating the same cursor against unchanged
310	data returns the byte-identical next page, and a newly captured snapshot
311	whose sort position is earlier never makes an already-returned record
312	resurface while the current page still follows the stable order.
313	`next_cursor` is the position after the page's last snapshot when at least
314	one follows and `null` otherwise; `has_more` is `true` exactly then and
315	`false` on both an empty and a last page. The query is strictly read-only
316	and machine-isolated — another machine's snapshots never enter the result
317	— and the body is compact UTF-8 JSON terminated by a single newline, free
318	of floating-point, `-0.0`, or non-finite values, byte-identical on repeat
319	calls against unchanged data, and readable for snapshots persisted across
320	application restarts.

322	
323	## Machine suspension and reactivation
324	
325	A machine is persistently either `active` (the status assigned at creation) or
326	`suspended`. `POST /machines/{machine_id}/status` with body
327	`{"status": "active"}` or `{"status": "suspended"}` changes it. The body must
328	be an object carrying a string `status` whose value is exactly `active` or
329	`suspended`; a missing body, non-object body, missing or non-string `status`,
330	or any other value returns `422` before the machine is looked up (so the same
331	payload against a non-existent machine is still `422`). A missing machine
332	returns `404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}`. Requesting the machine's current
333	status returns `409 {"error":{"code":"invalid_status_transition"}}` and writes
334	nothing, so concurrent requests for the same target status have at most one
335	success: the lookup, same-status check, and update run in one locked write
336	transaction. On success only `status` and `updated_at` change — `version`,
337	`public_key`, `created_at`, and every other record are untouched — and the
338	full updated machine object is returned with `200`. The status is stored in
339	the machines table and survives restarts.
340	
341	While a machine is `suspended`, both
342	`POST /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-evaluations` and
343	`POST /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-decision-events` return
344	`{"allowed": false, "reason": "machine_suspended"}` without consulting its
345	behavior declarations or the policy rules. Decision-event requests still
346	persist one event under the usual rules, linked into the machine's event hash
347	chain. After reactivation the normal declaration/policy evaluation resumes;
348	events recorded earlier (including while suspended) keep their stored result.
349	
350	The status determination, declaration/policy computation, and event append
351	for a decision-event request are one indivisible authorization write,
352	serialized against status changes by the same locked transaction, so two
353	concurrent requests (one status change and one event append) have a single
354	definite serial order and at most one can "win" a given target transition:
355	
356	- when the status change commits first, the later event reads the new status
357	  and uses its result — after a suspension the event is `machine_suspended`,
358	  never a result computed from the pre-change `active` state;
359	- when the event append commits first, it keeps the pre-change authorization
360	  result and the later status change never rewrites, recomputes, or
361	  reinterprets the committed event; once a status update completes, later
362	  event requests can no longer write a result based on the old `active`
363	  state.
364	
365	Concurrent execution never loses events, forks or breaks the hash chain, or
366	leaves a half-finished status or event record: the lookup, decision, and
367	append either commit together or leave no trace. Body validation (`422`) and
368	the missing-machine/path-resource (`404 not_found`) outcomes are unchanged by
369	this serialization and never flip error types under a status race.
370	
371	## Machine status history
372	
373	Every accepted status change appends exactly one immutable record to the
374	`machine_status_events` table inside the same locked write transaction that
375	updates the machine, so the status update and its history record commit
376	together or not at all. History records are never updated, deleted, or
377	recomputed afterwards, and the table is created automatically at startup on
378	databases that predate the feature, without touching existing records.
379	
380	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/status-history` returns the machine's own
381	transition records as a JSON array — empty when the machine has never changed
382	status. The query accepts no parameters: any query parameter (or request
383	body) is a `422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_query"}}` raised before the machine
384	is looked up, a missing machine is `404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}`, and
385	only `GET` is routed (other methods, including `HEAD`, return `405`). Each
386	item carries the five transition fields `{id, machine_id, from_status,
387	to_status, created_at}` in this fixed field order, with `created_at` the UTC
388	commit-moment stamp ending in `Z`, followed in the same positions by the
389	per-machine tamper-evident chain fields `previous_status_event_id`,
390	`content_hash`, and `chain_hash` described below. Records are ordered by the
391	actual UTC instant of `created_at`, then by `id`. The response body is
392	compact UTF-8 JSON terminated by a single newline and contains no
393	floating-point or non-finite values. The query only reads: it never creates,
394	updates, deletes, repairs, or normalizes status, history, or any other
395	record, and another machine's records never enter the result.
396	
397	## Machine status-history integrity chain
398	
399	Each machine's status-history records form a per-machine, tamper-evident
400	hash chain. Every record returned by the status-history list endpoint
401	carries, after its five transition fields:
402	
403	- `previous_status_event_id` — `null` for the machine's first record,
404	  otherwise the id of the preceding record in `(created_at, id)` order (the
405	  actual UTC instant, then id);
406	- `content_hash` — `SHA-256(UTF-8(compact key-sorted JSON of {id,
407	  machine_id, from_status, to_status, created_at}))`, covering the record
408	  identifier, machine ownership, the status edge, and the creation moment;
409	- `chain_hash` — `SHA-256(UTF-8("" + ":" + content_hash))` for the first
410	  record and `SHA-256(UTF-8(previous_chain_hash + ":" + content_hash))`
411	  thereafter.
412	
413	All hashes are 64-character lowercase hexadecimal strings. The existing
414	status fields, record id, from/to statuses, and creation moment are kept
415	exactly as stored and are never rewritten for a chain check. Each machine is
416	an independent chain: a record never points across machines or skips a link,
417	the first record is rooted at the empty prefix, and later records must link
418	to their immediate predecessor in the actual-UTC-instant/`id` order. A
419	successful status change updates the machine, appends the history record,
420	and links it to this machine's chain tail inside the existing single locked
421	write transaction, so concurrent same-target changes still have at most one
422	success and cannot lose records, fork the chain, or break a link. On
423	startup the service adds the new columns to pre-existing databases and
424	backfills missing chain data in `(created_at, id)` order; the recomputation
425	is deterministic, so restarting with an already complete database performs
426	no writes, and an empty database is directly usable.
427	
428	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/status-history/integrity` is the read-only
429	independent verification `integrity` sub-entry under the machine status
430	history path and returns the three integrity conclusions
431	`{valid, checked_count, broken_status_event_id}`: an empty or fully sound
432	chain reports `true`, the total count, and `null`; otherwise it reports
433	`false`, the total count, and the first record whose creation moment,
434	identifier, machine attribution, status edge, predecessor link, content
435	hash, or chain hash does not verify. The status edge must keep the existing
436	active/suspended semantics: both ends inside `active`/`suspended`, no self
437	loop, and each edge's `from_status` must continue the state the earlier
438	transitions establish (a machine is created `active`, and accepted changes
439	alternate). A record with a corrupted `created_at` still enters the total
440	and is itself reported as broken; a damaged record is never crashed on,
441	repaired, rewritten, or recomputed, and another machine's damaged records
442	never affect this machine's conclusion.
443	
444	The endpoint accepts no query parameters and no request body — either is a
445	`422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_query"}}` validated before the machine is
446	looked up and before any history is read (the same malformed request
447	against a non-existent machine is still `422`). After validation a missing
448	machine returns `404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}` with no partial
449	conclusion; a real failure while reading the history returns
450	`500 {"error":{"code":"internal_error"}}`, likewise with no partial
451	conclusion. Only `GET` is routed; `HEAD` and every other method return
452	`405` without reading history, computing a chain conclusion, or writing
453	anything. The query is strictly read-only and machine-isolated, repeated
454	queries of unchanged data are byte-identical compact UTF-8 JSON terminated
455	by a single newline with no floating-point or non-finite value, and the
456	conclusion persists across restarts.
457	
458	## Read-only machine status-history compliance export
459	
460	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/status-history/compliance-export` returns a
461	deterministic, read-only slice of one machine's status transition history
462	over a closed UTC time window. Only `GET` is routed (other methods,
463	including `HEAD`, return `405` without reading records). Both query
464	parameters are required and every check runs before the machine is looked
465	up, so a parameter error against a non-existent machine is still `422`:
466	
467	- `from_created_at`, `to_created_at` — UTC RFC 3339 date-times ending in `Z`
468	  (fractional seconds optional; offset forms such as `+00:00`, surrounding
469	  whitespace, and out-of-range calendar/time values are rejected);
470	  `from_created_at` must not be later than `to_created_at` (equal bounds are
471	  allowed). A missing, blank, malformed, or inverted bound returns
472	  `422 {"error":{"code":"bad_time"}}`.
473	- An unknown parameter, a repeated `from_created_at`/`to_created_at`, or a
474	  request body returns `422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_query"}}`.
475	
476	After validation, a missing machine returns
477	`404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}`; a real read failure returns
478	`500 {"error":{"code":"internal_error"}}` with no partial records.
479	
480	The response is `{machine_id, from_created_at, to_created_at,
481	status_history}` in this fixed key order; the machine id and the original
482	bound text are echoed verbatim, and `status_history` is an empty array
483	(never omitted) for an empty window, a machine with no history, or an empty
484	database. The array contains only the path machine's existing transition
485	records whose own `created_at` falls inside the closed interval, each with
486	the five transition fields `{id, machine_id, from_status, to_status,
487	created_at}` exactly as stored — the export keeps this five-field shape and
488	does not add the list endpoint's chain fields — ordered by the actual UTC
489	instant of `created_at` and then by record id — an exact-second record sorts
490	before any fractional-second record of the same second. A stored
491	`created_at` that no longer parses sorts after every parseable instant and
492	therefore never enters a finite window; damaged field values inside
493	in-window records are kept exactly as stored, never filtered, repaired, or
494	normalized. The query adds no persistence surface, repeats byte-identically,
495	reads across restarts, and never returns another machine's records.
496	
497	## Read-only machine behavior-declaration compliance export
498	
499	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/behavior-declarations/compliance-export` returns a
500	deterministic, read-only slice of one machine's behavior declarations over a
501	closed UTC creation-time window. It is a separate audit entry point under the
502	machine behavior-declaration path: declaration creation, the declaration list,
503	the declaration integrity audit, authorization evaluation, the event chains,
504	diagnostics, and the health check are unchanged, this endpoint never
505	participates in an evaluation and adds no way to write a declaration other than
506	the creation entry, and it adds no on-disk format, so old and empty databases
507	work unchanged. Only `GET` is routed (other methods, including `HEAD`, return
508	`405` without reading or filtering declarations or writing anything). Both
509	query parameters are required and every check runs before the machine is looked
510	up, so a parameter error against a non-existent machine is still `422`:
511	
512	- `from_created_at`, `to_created_at` — UTC RFC 3339 date-times ending in `Z`
513	  (fractional seconds optional; offset forms such as `+00:00`, surrounding
514	  whitespace, and out-of-range calendar/time values are rejected);
515	  `from_created_at` must not be later than `to_created_at` (equal bounds are
516	  allowed). A missing, blank, malformed, or inverted bound returns
517	  `422 {"error":{"code":"bad_time"}}`.
518	- An unknown parameter, a repeated `from_created_at`/`to_created_at`, or a
519	  request body returns `422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_query"}}`.
520	
521	After validation, a missing machine returns
522	`404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}`; a real read failure returns
523	`500 {"error":{"code":"internal_error"}}` with no partial records.
524	
525	The response is `{machine_id, from_created_at, to_created_at,
526	behavior_declarations}` in this fixed key order; the machine id and the
527	original bound text are echoed verbatim, and `behavior_declarations` is an
528	empty array (never omitted) for an empty window, a machine with no
529	declarations, or an empty database. The array contains only the path machine's
530	existing declarations whose own `created_at` falls inside the closed interval,
531	each with the complete list-view visible fields `{id, machine_id, action_type,
532	resource_pattern, enabled, created_at, updated_at}` exactly as stored — the
533	export adds no chain field — ordered by the actual UTC instant of `created_at`
534	and then by record id, so an exact-second record sorts before any
535	fractional-second record of the same second. A stored `created_at` that no
536	longer parses keeps its original text, deterministically sorts after every
537	parseable instant, and therefore never enters a finite window; illegal,
538	duplicated, missing, or otherwise damaged field values inside in-window records
539	are kept exactly as stored, never filtered, repaired, or normalized, and a
540	damaged association never drops the record. The query adds no persistence
541	surface, repeats byte-identically against unchanged data, reads across
542	restarts, and never returns another machine's declarations.

544	## Read-only joint-write transaction diagnostics
545	
546	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/diag` exposes read-only observability over the
547	joint write transaction shared by the status-change and decision-event
548	entries above. Every attempt at `POST /machines/{machine_id}/status` or
549	`POST /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-decision-events` produces exactly
550	one diagnostic record; the diagnostics feature adds no new write entry, and
551	the two README-documented endpoints remain the only way to change a machine's
552	status or create a decision event.
553	
554	Both query parameters are required and validated before the machine is
555	looked up, so an invalid query against a non-existent machine is still `422`:
556	
557	- `from`, `to` — UTC RFC 3339 date-times ending in `Z` (fractional seconds
558	  optional; offset forms such as `+00:00`, a missing suffix, surrounding
559	  whitespace, and out-of-range calendar/time values are rejected); `from`
560	  must not be later than `to` (equal bounds are allowed). A missing, blank,
561	  malformed, offset, or inverted bound returns
562	  `422 {"error":{"code":"bad_time"}}`.
563	- Any other query parameter returns `422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_query"}}`.
564	
565	After validation, a missing machine returns `404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}`.
566	
567	Success returns `200` with `{id, from, to, records, check}`: `id` is the path
568	machine id, `from`/`to` echo the bounds verbatim, and `check` is the machine's
569	current authorization-event integrity audit in the existing
570	`{valid, checked_count, broken_event_id}` shape. Each item in `records` is:
571	
572	- `tid` — the diagnostic record id;
573	- `at` — the terminal timestamp of the attempt, a UTC RFC 3339 date-time
574	  ending in `Z`;
575	- `op` — `change` for a status change, `event` for a decision-event creation;
576	- `phase` — `started-commit` (the joint write committed) or
577	  `started-rollback` (it rolled back; includes the attempt start and the
578	  terminal state);
579	- `fail` — `none` for every commit; a rollback carries one stable category:
580	  `race` (a concurrency conflict, including the losing request of a
581	  same-target status race), `io` (a persistence failure), or `other` (any
582	  other failure or a crash rollback);
583	- `flags` — `[]`, or the actually-experienced `lock_wait` and `retry` flags
584	  in that order. A lock wait and its retries collapse into this one record;
585	  a rollback is never recorded as a partial/fragmented entry;
586	- `status` — the attempt's **transaction terminal state**, exactly
587	  `committed` (the joint write landed) or `rolled_back` (it did not);
588	- `machine_status` — the machine's own terminal state for the attempt,
589	  `active` or `suspended` (the empty string for an attempt whose machine did
590	  not exist). It is deliberately separate from the transaction outcome, so a
591	  rolled-back attempt can still observe a `suspended` machine (for example,
592	  the losing request of a same-target suspension race reports
593	  `status = "rolled_back"` with `machine_status = "suspended"`);
594	- `event` — the created decision-event id for a committed `event` attempt,
595	  otherwise `null`;
596	- `count` — the machine's decision-event count at the terminal state (the
597	  event's chain position for a committed event attempt);
598	- `check` — the event hash-chain audit snapshot
599	  (`{valid, checked_count, broken_event_id}`) at the terminal state.
600	
601	Records contain only this operational metadata — never keys, secrets, policy
602	text, or identity material. `records` includes only finalized records owned by
603	the path machine whose `at` falls inside the closed interval `[from, to]`,
604	ordered by the actual UTC instant of `at` and then by `tid` (ISO-8601 text is
605	not chronological across the fractional-second boundary, so instants are
606	parsed first). If the process dies mid-attempt, the residual record is
607	finalized on the next startup from committed evidence — a decision event at
608	or after the attempt start for an event attempt, a fresh machine
609	`updated_at` for a status change — and classified as a commit or a crash
610	rollback; nothing is ever left half-finished.
611	
612	The query is strictly read-only: it never writes, repairs, recomputes, or
613	deletes diagnostics or any business record, gives identical results on repeat
614	calls against unchanged data, is stable across restarts (the startup recovery
615	pass finalizes residuals once and an already-complete database performs no
616	writes), and reads data persisted across restarts. Existing databases gain
617	the diagnostics table safely on startup, and an empty database is fully
618	usable. Databases created before the terminal-state split are migrated once
619	on startup: the old machine-state `status` value moves to `machine_status`
620	and `status` becomes the `committed`/`rolled_back` outcome derived from the
621	record's phase, so a second restart performs no writes. `422`/`404`/`409`,
622	the `active`/`suspended` semantics, and `GET /health` are unchanged.
623	
624	## Key rotation integrity chain
625	
626	Each machine's key rotation history forms its own per-machine, tamper-evident
627	hash chain, following the same rules as the authorization event integrity
628	chain. Every record returned by the key-rotation list endpoint carries:
629	
630	- `previous_rotation_id` — `null` for the machine's first rotation, otherwise
631	  the id of the preceding record in `(created_at, id)` order;
632	- `content_hash` — `SHA-256(UTF-8(compact key-sorted JSON of {id, machine_id,
633	  old_public_key, new_public_key, version, created_at}))`;
634	- `chain_hash` — `SHA-256(UTF-8("" + ":" + content_hash))` for the first
635	  record and `SHA-256(UTF-8(previous_chain_hash + ":" + content_hash))`
636	  thereafter.
637	
638	All hashes are 64-character lowercase hexadecimal strings. A successful
639	rotation updates the machine and appends the record to the chain tail inside
640	a single write transaction, so concurrent rotations cannot lose records,
641	fork, or break the chain. On startup the service adds the new columns to
642	pre-existing databases and backfills missing chain data in `(created_at, id)`
643	order; the recomputation is deterministic, so restarting with an already
644	complete database performs no writes.
645	
646	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/key-rotation-events/integrity` verifies the chain
647	read-only and returns `{valid, checked_count, broken_rotation_id}`: a complete
648	or empty chain reports `true`, the total count, and `null`; otherwise it
649	reports `false`, the total count, and the first record whose content hash,
650	link, or chain hash does not verify. The check never writes, repairs, or
651	deletes records, is stable across repeat calls and restarts, and only
652	examines the path machine's records. A missing machine returns
653	`404 not_found`.

655	## Read-only stable machine key-rotation incremental query
656	
657	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/key-rotation-events/changes` is the stable,
658	keyset-paginated incremental view over one machine's rotation records — the
659	`changes` sub-entry under the machine key-rotation record path. It is a
660	separate, strictly read-only audit entry point: it changes neither rotation
661	creation, the rotation list, the integrity audit, the compliance export, nor
662	any other machine interface, and it adds no on-disk format (cursors are
663	stateless), so old and empty databases work unchanged. The caller submits
664	only the path machine id, a page size, and an optional cursor — no business
665	filter parameters and no request body. Validation completes before the
666	machine or any rotation record is read:
667	
668	- `limit` — required, a non-boolean integer from `1` to `100`. A missing,
669	  blank, fractional (e.g. `1.0`), boolean (`true`/`false`), non-decimal,
670	  or out-of-range value returns `422 {"error":{"code":"bad_limit"}}`.
671	- `cursor` — optional, an opaque string shaped
672	  `<created_at original text>|<rotation id>` and returned by a previous
673	  page. An empty, non-string, or shape-mismatching value returns
674	  `422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_cursor"}}`; the timestamp segment is
675	  original stored text rather than re-parsed, because a rotation whose
676	  stored `created_at` no longer parses stays pageable. A well-shaped cursor
677	  whose `(created_at, id)` position cannot be located among the path
678	  machine's stored rotations (including a position naming another
679	  machine's record) is rejected as
680	  `422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_cursor"}}` while the records are read, so
681	  a parameter error always takes priority over the machine lookup.
682	- Any other query parameter, a repeated `limit`/`cursor`, or a request
683	  carrying a body returns `422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_query"}}` in the
684	  validation phase; every validation error is answered without reading any
685	  machine or rotation record.
686	- The path accepts `GET` only; other methods return `405` without reading
687	  records, computing a page, or writing anything.
688	- A valid query against a machine that does not exist returns
689	  `404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}` carrying no rotation records.
690	- A failure that prevents reading the records or the machine returns
691	  `500 {"error":{"code":"internal_error"}}` with no partial page.
692	
693	The success object carries exactly `{machine_id, limit, records,
694	next_cursor, has_more}` in this fixed field order; an empty database and a
695	machine with no rotations return the complete empty page. `records`
696	contains only rotations owned by the path machine, each with exactly the
697	complete fields of the rotation list view — the six visible fields `{id,
698	machine_id, old_public_key, new_public_key, version, created_at}` emitted
699	exactly as stored plus `previous_rotation_id`, `content_hash`, and
700	`chain_hash` — with no filtering, repair, or normalization. Records are
701	ordered by the actual UTC instant of `created_at` and then by record id
702	ascending, so an exact-second record sorts before any fractional-second
703	record of the same second. A stored `created_at` that no longer parses
704	never crashes the query: the record is kept with its stored value and
705	deterministically sorts after every parseable instant rather than being
706	deleted; damaged, missing, misowned, or duplicated chain values are
707	likewise emitted exactly as stored.
708	
709	The cursor is an exclusive position over `(created_at, rotation id)`: it
710	points just after a page's last record, so the page returns only records
711	strictly after it. Repeating the same cursor against unchanged data returns
712	the byte-identical next page, and a newly inserted rotation whose sort
713	position is earlier never makes an already-returned record resurface while
714	the current page still follows the stable order. `next_cursor` is the
715	position after the page's last record when at least one record follows and
716	`null` otherwise; `has_more` is `true` exactly when a record exists after
717	the current position and `false` on both an empty and a last page.
718	
719	The query is strictly read-only and machine-isolated: it never creates,
720	updates, deletes, repairs, recomputes, or normalizes a rotation, and another
721	machine's records never enter the result. The body is compact UTF-8 JSON
722	terminated by a single newline, free of floating-point, `-0.0`, or
723	non-finite values, byte-identical on repeat calls against unchanged data,
724	and readable for records persisted across application restarts.

738	- `evidence_type` is a string that stays non-empty after trimming surrounding

752	## Evidence tamper-evident chain and read-only chain verification
753	
754	In addition to the standalone evidence fingerprint and the read-only evidence
755	integrity audit above, each machine's evidence records form their own
756	per-machine, tamper-evident hash chain. The chain sits on the existing
757	machine-event evidence path: registering evidence keeps the same request
758	shape and, on success, appends the new record to the tail of **this machine's**
759	chain. Each record returned by the create, list, and evidence export
760	endpoints carries, in the same positions across all three:
761	
762	- `previous_evidence_id` — `null` for the machine's first evidence record,
763	  otherwise the id of the immediately preceding record in `(created_at, id)`
764	  order (the actual UTC instant, then id);
765	- `chain_hash` — the chain digest;
766	- the existing `content_hash` evidence fingerprint, unchanged.
767	
768	The per-record content digest is
769	`SHA-256(UTF-8(compact key-sorted JSON of {id, machine_id, event_id,
770	evidence_type, content_hash, created_at}))`, covering the record identifier,
771	machine, associated event, evidence type, fingerprint, and creation time. The
772	`chain_hash` is `SHA-256(UTF-8("" + ":" + content_digest))` for the first
773	record and `SHA-256(UTF-8(previous_chain_hash + ":" + content_digest))`
774	thereafter. All hashes are 64-character lowercase hexadecimal strings. Each
775	machine is an independent chain: a record never points across machines, the
776	first record is rooted at the empty prefix, and no two records share a
777	predecessor.
778	
779	The machine/event ownership lookup, the duplicate-fingerprint check, the
780	insert, and the chain-tail append run inside one locked write transaction —
781	the same lock the other per-machine chains take — so concurrent registrations
782	cannot lose records, skip a link, point two records at the same predecessor,
783	or fork the chain; the committed result is equivalent to one definite serial
784	order. Validation outcomes are unchanged: an illegal body is
785	`422` (before any path lookup), a missing machine/event or an event owned by
786	another machine is `404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}`, and a repeated
787	fingerprint on the same event is `409 {"error":{"code":"duplicate_evidence"}}`
788	with nothing written. On startup the service adds the new columns to
789	pre-existing databases and backfills missing chain data in stable
790	`(created_at, id)` order; the recomputation is deterministic, so restarting
791	with an already complete database performs no writes, and an empty database
792	can still register and query evidence.
793	
794	The evidence list returns only the path machine/event's records in stable
795	order, an empty array (`[]`) when there are none, as compact UTF-8 JSON
796	terminated by a single newline; the body contains no floating-point, `-0.0`,
797	or non-finite value, counts stay JSON integers, and field order is stable
798	across calls.
799	
800	`GET /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-decision-events/evidence-chain/integrity`
801	verifies the whole evidence chain read-only and returns the existing evidence
802	audit's three conclusions,
803	`{valid, checked_count, broken_evidence_id}`: it applies the existing checks
804	(event ownership, non-blank `evidence_type`, exact lowercase-hex fingerprint
805	compared as stored) **and** verifies each record's content digest, its
806	`previous_evidence_id` link, and its `chain_hash`. A complete or empty chain
807	reports `true`, the total count, and `null` (an empty chain reports `true`,
808	`0`, `null`); otherwise it reports `false`, the machine's total evidence
809	count, and the first record whose content, link, or chain digest does not
810	verify. A record whose `created_at` is corrupted still parses into the total
811	and is reported as broken; a missing associated record never removes the
812	evidence row; another machine's damaged records never affect this machine's
813	conclusion. Only the first error is reported and nothing is repaired. The
814	endpoint accepts no query parameters — any parameter is
815	`422 {"error":{"code":"invalid_query"}}` raised before the machine is looked
816	up — a missing machine returns `404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}` with no
817	partial chain conclusion, and only `GET` is routed (other methods return
818	`405` without reading records). The query produces no writes and repeated
819	calls against unchanged data return byte-identical results. Existing events,
820	key rotation, incidents, diagnostics, and export filtering semantics are
821	unchanged.

854	## Incident status transitions and immutable history
855	
856	An incident moves through a fixed state machine: `open` (the status assigned
857	at registration) → `acknowledged` → `resolved`.
858	
859	`POST /machines/{machine_id}/authorization-decision-events/{event_id}/incidents/{incident_id}/status`
860	advances one incident. The body is `{"status": "..."}` where `status` must be
861	the string `"acknowledged"` or `"resolved"`; a missing field, a non-string
862	value, or any other string returns `422`, and body validation runs before any
863	path lookup (so a malformed payload is `422` even when nothing on the path
864	exists). After validation, the machine, event, and incident must all exist and
865	belong to one another; a missing one or an ownership mismatch returns
866	`404 {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}`. Only `open → acknowledged` and
867	`acknowledged → resolved` are legal; any other transition returns
868	`409 {"error":{"code":"invalid_status_transition"}}` and writes nothing. On
869	success the incident's `status` is updated and one history record is appended
870	inside a single transaction (so the two can never diverge, and concurrent
871	transitions cannot both observe the same prior status); the record is linked
872	into the machine's incident-status-event hash chain in the same transaction,
873	so the status, the record, and its chain link commit together or not at all.
874	The response is `200` with the full updated incident (the same fields as the
875	incident create/list endpoints).
876	
877	`GET .../incidents/{incident_id}/status-history` returns the incident's
878	immutable transition records in `created_at`, then `id` order (`[]` for an
879	incident that has never moved). The machine, event, and incident are validated
880	exactly as for the POST, including the same `404 not_found` outcomes. Each
881	entry contains exactly `{id, machine_id, event_id, incident_id, from_status,
882	to_status, created_at, previous_status_event_id, content_hash, chain_hash}`:
883	a fresh UUID `id`, `created_at` a UTC RFC 3339 date-time ending in `Z`, and
884	the per-machine chain fields described below. History rows are append-only —
885	they are never updated or deleted, so a rejected transition leaves the
886	incident status and the history both untouched, and neither endpoint ever
887	writes or modifies events, evidence, hash chains, or causal links. History is
888	strictly isolated to its own incident (another incident, event, or machine
889	can never read it) and persists across application restarts.
